name: vix_adjusted_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Standard VWAP mean reversion uses fixed thresholds (e.g., z-score < -1.5). But the optimal z-score threshold varies with VIX regime: in low VIX (< 14), even -1.0 z-score is a tradeable dislocation. In high VIX (> 20), you need -2.5+ z-score because dislocations are larger but also more noise. This adaptive strategy adjusts the entry z-score threshold based on current VIX level, capturing more trades in calm markets and being more selective in volatile markets. Edge persists because adaptive thresholds require continuous calibration that fixed-rule traders don't implement.

indicators.name: adaptive_threshold
indicators.formula: 1.0 + (vix - 12) * 0.1 (scales from 1.0 at VIX=12 to 2.0 at VIX=22)

exit.stop_loss: 1.5 * adaptive_threshold in z-score terms OR 1.5 * atr_20 in price terms
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to BE after z-score crosses halfway back

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days, expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — adaptive thresholds are more robust to regime changes than fixed ones

weaknesses: The linear scaling formula (1.0 + (vix-12)*0.1) is arbitrary — optimal mapping needs calibration
In VIX transitional zones, the threshold may flip between bars causing erratic behavior
Adding VIX dependence to the threshold adds a parameter that could be overfit
prior_art: Adaptive mean reversion — combining VWAP z-score with VIX regime. Novel parametrization.
notes: Calibrate the adaptive_threshold formula using walk-forward optimization on 2018-2023 data.
